newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Grey Advertising set to buy France's BDDP.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Grey Advertising set to buy France's BDDP.

text.p: New York ad agency Grey Advertising is set to acquire France's third biggest advertising group Boulet Dru Dupuy Petit (BDDP), industry sources said Wednesday.
"The dossier has been sent to all the majors in the industry and in the end it is Grey Advertising who is going to seal the deal," a source said.
BDDP's management is also interested in acquiring the company but sources said Grey was the clear front-runner.

Walter Butler, the investor who leads the European Strategic Investment (ESI) fund which has 20 percent of BDDP and heads an alliance of investors controlling 46 percent of the company, had no comment on the information.
Butler has been looking for a buyer for BDDP for some time and in May he met Grey Advertising boss Ed Meyer who is interested in BDDP's U.S. unit Wells Rich Greene.
Butler led a group of investors in 1993 to buy up the loss-making ad agency. The group posted a profit of 65 million francs last year and Butler is now trying to sell.
Industry sources said that the Grey deal would be concluded at $150 million at maximum, much below the $200 million originally sought by Butler.
Other candidates for the buy were Maurice & Charles Saatchi and WPP Group Plc but they dropped out of negotiations.
Cordiant Plc in July denied being interested in the group.
Wells Rich has major accounts such as Procter & Gamble.
